svg.title: iOS · Guided clip (experimental) · closing step · portrait
svg.desc: Mirrors App/GuidedBuilderView.swift (stretchStep for the closing base run: transitionCard + closingDefaultCard, columnLayout). Step 3 of 4 since Canvas and Opening merged (2026-08-12 UX sign-off) — the rail on wide surfaces calls this row "Ending"; the dots keep the question's own words. The labelled progress line ("Step 3 of 4 · Ending") sits under the dots and the title is absolutely centred (FlowHeader centersTitle) so the EXPERIMENTAL capsule cannot displace it. Question "How does it end?". The transition question is ALWAYS asked — the ramp back out of the last moment is part of the answer even when the closing state is the default — so HOW IT ARRIVES sits above the default card (Step "hard cut" active here; choosing an ease welds the punch-out framing move to the same ramp). The closingDefaultCard: arrow.uturn.backward glyph, 15pt semibold "Ends like it starts" (reads "Ends wide" instead when the opening carries a punch — the default closing state is always wide + the opening's speed), 12pt secondary "Wide · 50× smooth — tap Next to keep it." (speed via WarpTimeline.speedLabel + speedWord, synced from the opening on leaving step one — only when the LAST stretch is a base run; a shoot that ends on a recorded moment gets the moment question instead and keeps its seeded ¼×), and the accent "Change…" link which reveals the full speed + framing controls (closingOverride). The sync also never fires once the closing speed already differs from the opening (a deliberate override read back on re-entry). Next lands on Review. NEW (2026-08-12, guided scrub previews): the column layout keeps a picture on the ending — under the default card, columnWideStage centres the output-shaped exact-frame stage wrapped in GuidedScrubOverlay (App/GuidedScrubPreview.swift): a GuidedCanvasFrame of the very frame the clip ends on (ExactFrameLoader, badge "Stretch 2 — exact · as shot"; allowsReposition false — off the canvas step a drag never moves the clip's crop), sized CollectionMath.fit(canvas aspect, max 190×300) → 169×300 for this as-shot 9:16 shoot. 8pt under it, exactly the pane's width, the GuidedScrubStrip: a 22pt white card capsule (primary-8% hairline) covering the ending stretch's slice of the finished clip's clock — 9pt semibold secondary end labels "19s" and "21s" (window start / end+1 over outputFPS; the clip's own zero renders "0s") flanking the idle affordance, an eye glyph + "Preview" in 10pt semibold LL.accent, centred. Below, wideStageCaption for the closing role: "Ends wide — the whole canvas." (11.5pt secondary hint, leading-aligned with the pane). Desc-only states, not drawn: SCRUBBED — dragging the strip (or the pane itself: allowsPaneScrub, GuidedPaneScrub's axis-classified drag so a vertical scroll still wins on iOS) swaps the pane's picture for GuidedScrubDisplay, the ≈ keyframe preview at the scrubbed moment shown through the render's crop with a bottom-leading black-55% capsule badge "≈ preview · 20s of 21s" (white bold 10pt), while a 14pt LL.accent knob with a 1.5pt white ring rides the strip in place of the Preview label; LOCKED — a finished drag holds the preview and an xmark.circle.fill (15pt, secondary) appears trailing OUTSIDE the bar to let it go; macOS hover-to-peek scrubs on strip/pane hover and clears on exit unless locked. Captured from the iPhone 17 Pro sim, mapped onto the 393×852 canvas.

g.text: One ramp — the speed change and the framing move ride it
together, in seconds of the finished clip.
Wide · 50× smooth — tap Next to keep it.
